summary: Intermittent duplicate top-k + 500s on rerank after shard embedding-dimension drift during rollout
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-12 08:00 UTC LexiSearch reports intermittent 500s from the /rerank endpoint and repeated duplicate entries in top-k results for some queries.
Impact: customer search relevance is degraded and production latency spikes to >6s for affected requests.
Environment: Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-lexi), us-east region, rolling rollout in progress for embedding-worker images.
Observed behavior:
- Rerank returns HTTP 500 for ~2-5% of requests during peak.
- When successful, top-k contains duplicated document IDs and duplicated scores in positions 1..5 for some queries.
- Spike correlates with the running of a canary/rollout that updated embedding-worker to a new build with lightweight quantization metadata change.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Send a batch rerank request (batch size 64) with precomputed embeddings (text-embed-large-v2) routed through the dedicated pool.
2) Interleave payloads that include embeddings produced before and after the customer's most recent embedding-worker rollout.
3) Observe duplicated top-k IDs and occasional 500s in response.
Logs / examples:
- reranker: ERROR input validation failed: embedding length mismatch (expected 1536, got 1535)
- router: WARN shard=shard-17 accepted payload with header.embed-dim=1535
- embedding-worker-shard-17: INFO wrote vector header version=2.1; dims=1535
- embed-cache: WARN cache hit mismatch; key=doc:8421 expected-dims=1536 actual-dims=1535
comments: 2026-03-12 09:05 - Support (Aisha): Customer reported sudden duplicate top-k and intermittent 500s starting during their scheduled dedicated rollout. They attached request IDs and a small payload sample.

2026-03-12 10:30 - SRE (Marco): Reproduced locally by mixing embeddings emitted by two different worker images. Observed schema header mismatch (dim header 1535 vs 1536). Raised hypothesis that a lightweight quantization change incorrectly updated header calculation on a subset of shards.

2026-03-13 02:12 - Eng (Priya): Confirmed that a canary build (image-tag: embed-worker:v2026.3.11-quant) had a packaging script that trimmed trailing zero dimension when serializing in one code path. Rolling back that build on affected shard removed the 500s but duplicates persisted until we invalidated embed-cache for that shard.

2026-03-14 08:42 - Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed reduced errors after hotfix and cache invalidation. They still see isolated duplicates for queries that hit mixed replicas; requested permanent validation to prevent future schema drift.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 03-12 canary rollout -> errors start; 03-12 evening reproduce with mixed-embeddings; 03-13 found embed header off-by-one produced by new packaging path. Tools used: reproducer script against dedicated pool, tcpdump of router traffic, embed-cache inspection. Findings: - Router accepts vectors with header dims and forwards to reranker; reranker attempted best-effort alignment (pad/truncate) which produced duplicate IDs when padding applied inconsistently across replicas. - 500s occurred when reranker input validation refused to coerce unexpected length. Hypotheses: partial rollout left ~20% of shards with new serialization, producing mixed-dimension payloads in multiplexed requests. Evidence: file checksums of embed-worker binaries differ; shard assignment maps show affected shards: shard-17, shard-34, shard-42. Actions tried: rolled back embed-worker image on affected shards, invalidated embed-cache keys for those shards, applied a temporary request-level validation in router to reject mixed-dimension batches (400) instead of forwarding inconsistent payloads (prevents 500 but surface error). Monitoring: enabled per-shard embed-dim metrics and added alert on dimension-variance > 0.5%.
resolution: Workaround applied: rolled back canary image on affected shards and performed embed-cache invalidation; instructed customer to retry failing queries. Root cause: a packaging/serialization change in embed-worker (PR github.com/redwood-inference/embeddings/pull/278) trimmed a trailing dimension header for the quant path, producing 1535-dim vectors. Permanent fix: merged PR github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5254 which adds strict embed-dim validation at ingress and a graceful coercion path with logging and metrics. Follow-ups: (1) backfill: run a one-time verification job across dedicated pools to find mismatched cached embeddings; (2) add unit/integration tests to prevent header-trim regressions; (3) update rollout runbook to include embed-dim check and phased canary with embed-dim histogram monitoring. Customer status: LexiSearch accepted workaround and requested postmortem; SLA credits under review.
follow_up_actions: Run verification sweep across dedicated pools to detect cached mismatched embeddings
Add CI test to catch header-serialization regressions
Update rollout runbook to include embed-dim histogram and pre/post-checks
Provide postmortem to customer and offer SLA remediation if applicable
notes_for_support: If customer sees new 400s after fix, advise them that router will reject mixed-dimension batches and to regenerate embeddings with consistent worker versions. For immediate relief, support can temporarily route customer's traffic to a single pinned replica until embedding footprint is reconciled.
